title: market-moves payload
description: A dated price SERIES per admitted prediction market, from one venue, selected by market-moves/rule.yaml and nothing else. There is no moves[] block and no probability-shaped field anywhere in this schema, on purpose: a consumer derives moves itself (the twin's twin/market_signals.py price_moves), and a price level is a biased estimator of a probability with a known sign and an unmeasured scale (Buergi, Deng & Whelan 2026; twin research 17 S3.1), so nothing here may be read as a belief. The entry map is `markets`, keyed by the venue's own market id.

venue.description: Version 1 reads one venue. Kalshi lands as a minor bump under the same rule; corroboration is a consumer reading two series, never a publisher claim.

source.description: The venue endpoint this corpus was read from, verbatim.

selection_rule.description: The versioned mechanical rule that admitted these markets. A consumer re-derives the selection from the venue corpus and this rule; a change to it is a minor bump.

markets.description: Venue market id -> the market and its dated series. The KEY is the market id, so the id is carried exactly once.

question.description: The venue's own question text, verbatim.

category.description: The venue's own category. Carried so the selection is reproducible from the payload against rule.yaml.

resolution_source.description: Where the market resolves from, as the venue states it. This is the evidence grade of the series: a market resolving off an official statistic is not the same instrument as one resolving off a vote of holders.

observations.description: The dated series. Appended to, never overwritten.

price_level.description: The venue's traded price for the market's yes outcome, in [0,1]. A LEVEL, never a probability: twin/market_signals.py's as_probability refuses outright rather than converting.
